title: Samye
hook: the first monastery in Tibet, laid out as a mandala

segments.voice: Yesterday: Padmasambhava, who tamed the forces blocking the way. Your line: the obstacles tamed.

A story tells that when the king asked what his monastery would look like, Padmasambhava showed it to him, whole, in the palm of his hand. The king looked, and all he could say was: inconceivable! In Tibetan, samye. And that, the story goes, became the monastery's name. Hear it as history or as a beautiful way of saying it; either way, the place itself is laid out like nothing else around it. Seen from above, it looks like a diagram.
screen: `A MONASTERY IN A PALM.` → `INCONCEIVABLE.` → `FROM ABOVE, A DIAGRAM.`

segments.voice: Tibetan histories remember Samye as the first monastery in Tibet, raised under King Trisong Detsen with the abbot Shantarakshita and Padmasambhava. What makes it unusual is its plan. Samye was laid out as a mandala, a map of the universe as Buddhists in India pictured it. At the center rises the main temple, standing for Mount Meru, the great mountain at the middle of the world. Around it, smaller temples stand for the continents in each direction, with lesser shrines beside them. And around everything runs a round wall, the ring of mountains at the world's edge. So walking into Samye is walking into a picture of the cosmos, from the rim toward the center. A mandala may be familiar as a painting, or as a design laid out in colored sand. Samye makes it a place. Pilgrims walk around it, keeping the center on their right, each circuit drawing them around the middle, never straight at it. And the plan says something without a word: the center isn't alone, and the edge isn't outside. Everything, from the farthest wall to the middle shrine, belongs to one design. The histories add that the first Tibetan monks were ordained here, by the Indian abbot. So a story that began with an invitation now has a home: a building that teaches by its shape.
screen: `THE FIRST MONASTERY, THE HISTORIES SAY.` · `MOUNT MERU AT THE CENTER.` · `CONTINENTS, AND A ROUND WALL.` · `A BUILDING THAT TEACHES BY SHAPE.` · then, large: `A MONASTERY AS A MANDALA.`

segments.voice: With your eyes closed if that's comfortable, picture stepping through the gate of a round wall and walking slowly around the inside, the center on your right, coming a little closer with each circuit. At last, stand before the temple at the center and rest there with the breath; there's nothing to do at the center but arrive.
Samye. Inconceivable, the story says. Tibet's first monastery in the histories, laid out as a mandala, a map of the world you can walk around.
Your line: a monastery as a mandala. From the rim to the center, it's one design. Day nine hundred thirty-three, done.

howItsDone: Pilgrims to Samye walk clockwise around the monastery and its central temple, and Tibetan Buddhists make mandalas in paint and colored sand as supports for meditation.
